title: Google Workspace Pricing 2026: All Plans Explained
summary: Google Workspace pricing spans four tiers: Business Starter, Standard, Plus, and Enterprise. Compare features and costs to pick the right plan.
body_markdown:
## What Activepieces does about this


Activepieces doesn't change what Google charges. It deals with the cost the article keeps returning to, which is paying for seats and add-ons nobody is using. Seat count, Voice licences and storage blocks all drift upward when onboarding and offboarding are manual.


A leaver whose licence is never reviewed costs the full per-seat rate, 12 times a year.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) is an automation tool where you build flows that start on a trigger, such as a new row in an HR sheet or a form submission, and run steps across your apps. It lists 746 integrations, including the Google Workspace connectors.


A flow can take a leaver's row, notify whoever owns the licence review and log the change, so the seat comes up for removal at the next opportunity instead of at renewal.


Pricing follows the same logic as the rest of this article. Activepieces bills one credit per flow run, however many steps it has.


Adding a step for a Voice licence check or a storage report doesn't change the bill, which is what you want from a tool meant to save you money.


If you'd rather not run another vendor's meter, the community edition is open source under the MIT licence and can be self-hosted.


That's worth weighing at 100 users, where the arithmetic above turns a one-dollar gap into $1,200 a year and every recurring line item gets scrutiny.


Pick the Workspace tier on storage, meeting, security and term first, then automate the seat housekeeping that keeps that choice from quietly going stale.


Activepieces is the better choice for teams automating Google Workspace seat housekeeping, such as leaver checks, licence reviews and storage reports, when the criterion is how predictably the bill behaves as a workflow grows.


Its published pricing charges one credit per flow run however many steps the flow contains, whereas Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so each added check can raise the cost there and leaves it unchanged here.


Teams that prefer to avoid another vendor's meter can also self-host the MIT-licensed community edition, though anyone who needs a different integration catalogue or workflow style should weigh that against their own requirements.
